content: 1. Atazanavir is contraindicated with rifapentine because rifapentine decreases atazanavir levels by increasing its metabolism through the CYP3A4 enzyme system. 2. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 3. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 4. Coadministration of atazanavir with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided if possible. 5. Atazanavir increases rosuvastatin levels through an unknown mechanism, potentially leading to increased toxicity, including myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. Limit rosuvastatin dose to 10 mg/day. The ritonavir component in atazanavir/ritonavir regimens decreases rosuvastatin metabolism. 6. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose of ruxolitinib to 10 mg twice daily if platelet count is ≥100 x 10^9/L and avoid use if platelet count is <100 x 10^9/L. 7. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of selpercatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce selpercatinib dosage as per specific recommendations and wait 3-5 half-lives of the discontinued drug before resuming the original selpercatinib dose. 8. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of selumetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the selumetinib dosage as per its monograph. 9. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of silodosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 10. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of siponimod by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors combined with moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitors. 11. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 12. Sodium bicarbonate decreases atazanavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Sodium citrate/citric acid decreases atazanavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Sotorasib decreases atazanavir levels by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, refer to the prescribing information for dosage modifications. 15. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of sparsentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment and consider dose titration when resuming. 16. St. John’s Wort decreases atazanavir levels by increasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 17. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of stiripentol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Atazanavir increases suvorexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Suvorexant is not recommended with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 19. Atazanavir increases tadalafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Stop tadalafil at least 24 hours before initiating a protease inhibitor (PI) and restart 7 days after PI initiation at 20 mg once daily, increasing to 40 mg once daily based on tolerability. 20. Atazanavir affects tamoxifen metabolism by inhibiting CYP3A4, reducing its conversion to the active metabolite N-desmethyl tamoxifen. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Atazanavir increases tamsulosin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to increased toxicity. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Atazanavir increases tazemetostat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 23. Tepotinib increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the P-gp substrate dosage as recommended in its product labeling. 24. Tipranavir increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 25. Atazanavir increases tofacitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg once daily when coadministered with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors. 26. Atazanavir increases tolvatptan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 27. Atazanavir increases trabectedin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor must be used, administer it 1 week after trabectedin infusion and discontinue it the day before the next infusion. 28. Atazanavir increases triazolam levels by inhibiting its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 29. Tucatinib increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose according to product labeling. 30. Atazanavir increases vemurafenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Atazanavir increases vilazodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the vilazodone dose to 20 mg daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 32. Vonoprazan decreases atazanavir levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 33. Atazanavir increases vorapaxar levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Voriconazole increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and atazanavir increases voriconazole levels by the same mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Atazanavir increases voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 36. Atazanavir and abacavir both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 37. Atazanavir increases abemaciclib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of abemaciclib is required. If the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, increase abemaciclib to the dose prior to initiating the inhibitor. 38. Atazanavir increases acalabrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Decrease the acalabrutinib dose to 100 mg once daily if coadministered with a moderate CYP3A inhibitor. 39. Atazanavir decreases acarbose effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor for new-onset or exacerbation of diabetes mellitus and hyperglycemia. 40. Atazanavir increases acebutolol effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Consider lowering the beta-blocker dose. 41. Atazanavir decreases albiglutide effects, potentially due to insulin resistance. Use caution and monitor for hyperglycemia. 42. Atazanavir increases almotriptan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 43. Atazanavir increases alprazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 44. Atazanavir increases amitriptyline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 45. Atazanavir increases amoxapine levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor. 46. Atazanavir increases apalutamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction may be needed based on tolerability. 47. Atazanavir increases aprepitant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 48. Atazanavir increases aripiprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 49. Atazanavir increases artemether levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to increased toxicity. Use alternatives if available. 50. Atazanavir increases artemether/lumefantrine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 51. Atazanavir increases atenolol effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Consider lowering the beta-blocker dose. 52. Atazanavir increases atogepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The recommended atogepant dosage is 10 mg once daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 53. Atazanavir increases atorvastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 54. Atazanavir may increase or decrease conjugated estrogen levels. Use alternatives if available. 55. Belzutifan decreases atazanavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, consider increasing the sensitive CYP3A4 substrate dose according to its prescribing information. 56. Atazanavir increases benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Berotralstat increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Monitor or titrate the P-gp substrate dose if coadministered. 58. Atazanavir increases betaxolol effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Consider lowering the beta-blocker dose. 59. Atazanavir increases bexarotene levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 60. Atazanavir increases bisoprolol effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Consider lowering the beta-blocker dose. 61. Atazanavir increases bortezomib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 62. Atazanavir increases brentuximab vedotin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor patients for adverse reactions. 63. Atazanavir increases brexpiprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Administer half the usual brexpiprazole dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If also coadministered with a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor, administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose. 64. Atazanavir increases bromocriptine levels by inhibiting its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 65. Atazanavir increases budesonide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 66. Atazanavir increases buprenorphine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 67. Atazanavir increases buprenorphine buccal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 68. Atazanavir increases buprenorphine subdermal implant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor patients for signs of overmedication. If the CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be reduced or discontinued, implant removal may be necessary, and the patient should be treated with a buprenorphine dosage form that allows dose adjustments.
